# search


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) sends
one query to several search engines and merges their results into one
list. Each engine finds pages that other engines miss. A page that
several engines rank highly usually gives a useful result. Fossick uses
[ddgs](https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs) to reach the engines. `ddgs` does
not need API keys.
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) merges
the lists with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF). It can then reorder the
merged list by query relevance.

[`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
loads the Google results page in a stealth browser. It is slower than
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search).
[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
searches, downloads readable results, and returns a markdown digest with
a citation for each source. You can pass the digest to a language model.

## The ddgs client

[`get_ddgs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#get_ddgs)
returns a shared `DDGS` client for each timeout and proxy setting. It
creates each client on first use.
[`ddgs_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#ddgs_env)
reads proxy and certificate settings from the environment. This supports
search behind a corporate proxy. It reads the proxy from `DDGS_PROXY`,
`HTTPS_PROXY` or `https_proxy`. It reads a certificate bundle from
`FOSSICK_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or
`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`.

## Asking each engine

For text search, Fossick queries each engine in `TEXT_BACKENDS`
separately. It keeps each engine’s results in that engine’s rank order.
It does not use `ddgs` combined search. That search picks engines at
random and favours Wikipedia.
[`backends`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#backends)
lists every `ddgs` engine for a category. When `pages` is greater than
1, Fossick asks each engine for that many result pages. It drops results
on later pages when they repeat earlier results. The test checks that
ranks continue across pages.

## Merging the lists

Reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) merges ranked lists without using the
engines’ own scores. The scores are not comparable. Each page gets
`1/(k + rank)` from each list that contains it. RRF adds these values. A
page ranked first scores more than a page ranked eighth. A page found by
several engines gets one value from each engine. `k` is 60 by default.
It controls how much more the top ranks count than the lower ranks.

[`rrf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rrf) treats
two URLs as the same page when they differ only in scheme, `www.`, a
trailing slash or tracking parameters. It uses
[`norm_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#norm_url)
from `fossick.quality`. For each page, it keeps the longest snippet. It
also keeps the fused `score` and `engines`, which lists the engines that
found the page.

## Reranking

Search engines use more than exact query words when they rank results.
[`rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rerank)
reorders results by how well their title, snippet and URL match the
query. It combines this relevance score with the merged score. `mix`
sets the weight of the merged score. Its default is 0.4. A value of 1
ignores the reranker. When `method` is not `'none'`,
[`rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rerank)
adds a
[`rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rerank)
field with the relevance score.

`method` selects the scorer. `'lexical'` uses BM25, a standard
word-matching formula.
[`bm25`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#bm25)
computes scores from the result list. It does not need a stored index.
`'flashrank'` uses the small cross-encoder model from
[flashrank](https://github.com/PrithivirajDamodaran/FlashRank). The
model reads the query and each result together. It matches meaning
better. It needs `pip install flashrank`.
[`flashrank_scores`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#flashrank_scores)
returns None when `flashrank` is missing. `method='flashrank'` then
raises `ImportError`. `'auto'` uses `flashrank` when installed and BM25
otherwise. `'none'`, the default for
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search), keeps
the merged order.

## Where and when

The best answer to many questions depends on the country. Building
rules, prices and availability differ by country. Search engines use a
`country-language` region code, such as `au-en`. The default
`region='auto'` reads both parts from the query.

[`infer_country`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_country)
looks for country names, adjectives and cities in `COUNTRY_WORDS`. It
answers only when the query names one country. A query that names two
countries returns None.
[`infer_language`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_language)
counts common function words in `LANG_WORDS`, such as “the” and “what”
or “der” and “und”. It answers only when one language has the highest
count and at least two matches.
[`infer_region`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_region)
joins the country and language results. A query with no language signal
uses the country’s usual language from `COUNTRY_LANG`. The default
`us-en` fills any part that the query does not define. An English
question about France gives `fr-en`.

`timelimit` keeps only recent results. Use `'d'`, `'w'`, `'m'` or `'y'`
for the past day, week, month or year.

## [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search)

[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) is the
main entry point. For text, it queries every engine in `TEXT_BACKENDS`
in parallel. It merges the lists with RRF and reranks them with
`method`. `backend='google'` restricts it to one engine. `n` cuts the
final list only. It does not change the number of engines queried.
Increase `pages` to get more candidates. With `fuse=False`, and for the
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images),
[`news`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#news) and
`books` categories, it uses `ddgs` search for that category. The
[`videos`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#videos)
category uses
[`search_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search_yt)
to search YouTube.

An empty query returns an empty list without using the network. When
every engine fails,
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) prints
one warning per process and returns an empty list. `text`,
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images),
[`news`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#news),
[`videos`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#videos) and
`books` are
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) with a
category set.
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#extract)
downloads one URL with `ddgs`. It returns `{url, content}`. The default
content format is markdown.

`cache=900` keeps a result in memory for 900 seconds. A later call with
the same arguments returns that result without a request. An empty
result is not kept. This prevents an outage result from being kept.
`fetch(cache=)` uses the same memory and the `MEM_MOST` limit.
[`forget()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#forget)
clears the memory. The default `cache=0` asks the engines on every call.

## [`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)

[`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
loads Google’s results page in the stealth browser and reads the results
from it. The ranking is Google’s own. It is slower than
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) and
needs Scrapling’s browsers. It accepts the same `region` and `timelimit`
as [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search).
The country biases the ranking. It does not exclude other countries.
Google applies the time limit with its own filter. The results have the
same fields as
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search). The
snippet is in `content`. When Google returns no results,
[`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
returns an empty list. When the browser fails, it returns an empty list
and prints a warning.

## [`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)

[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
turns a question into readable sources in five steps:

1.  [`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan),
    from `fossick.quality`, splits a question with several parts into
    one search per part. It keeps the original question as the first
    search.
2.  Each search uses
    [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search),
    or
    [`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
    when `engine='google'`.
    [`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
    interleaves the results by taking one result from each search in
    turn.
3.  The default `curated=True` makes
    [`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
    remove sites that copy other sites. It also moves authoritative
    sources up.
    [`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
    drops copycats before it downloads pages.
4.  [`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
    downloads candidates in order with `fetch(auto=True)`. Each batch
    contains as many pages as needed to reach `n`. It stops after it
    gets `n` pages with at least 400 characters of readable markdown. A
    failed, blocked or short page goes into `dropped` with its reason.
    The next candidate replaces it.
5.  With `focused=True`,
    [`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus)
    reduces each page to about `chars` characters from passages that
    best answer the question.

It returns a dictionary with `query`, `sources`, `digest`, `dropped`,
`region`, `curation` and
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan). Each
source contains its `title`, `href`, working fetch `tier`, publication
`date`, answered `queries` and markdown in `md`. The digest joins the
sources with `---`. Each source has its title, URL, publication date
when known and the question part it answers.

[`page_date`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#page_date),
[`usable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#usable) and
[`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus) also
work on their own.
[`page_date`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#page_date)
finds a page’s publication date and returns `YYYY-MM-DD`, or None. It
reads JSON-LD data, `<meta>` tags named in `DATE_META`, a `<time>`
element or a `/2018/09/` URL.
[`usable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#usable)
checks for a 200 response, no bot wall and at least `min_chars`
characters of readable markdown. `min_chars=0` skips the length check.
[`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus) keeps
passages that answer a query. It keeps opening blocks within 30% of the
character budget. It then adds the highest-scoring blocks. It returns
them in their original order and uses `…` for gaps.

The next cell tests paging with stand-in engines.

``` python
# Keep ranks continuous across pages and count repeated results once.
_seen = []
def _fake(be, q, region='us-en', page=1, timeout=8, tries=2, **kw):
    _seen.append((be, page))
    start = (page-1)*2
    return [dict(title=f'{be}{i}', href=f'https://e.com/{be}/{i}', body='', engine=be, rank=i-start+1)
            for i in range(start, start+3)]        # Return three hits per page and repeat one hit on the next page.
_real, _engine_hits = _engine_hits, _fake
try:
    one = _backend_lists('q', ('brave',), pages=1)
    two = _backend_lists('q', ('brave',), pages=2)
    later = _backend_lists('q', ('brave',), page=3)
finally: _engine_hits = _real

assert sorted(_seen[:3]) == [('brave',1), ('brave',1), ('brave',2)], _seen   # Run one job for each backend and page.
assert _seen[3:] == [('brave',3)]                                        # Start paging at `page`.
assert len(one[0]) == 3 and len(two[0]) == 5                             # Two pages return five unique results.
assert [h['rank'] for h in two[0]] == [1,2,3,4,5]                        # Use continuous ranks.
assert len({h['href'] for h in two[0]}) == 5                             # Remove duplicates within the backend.
```

## Tests

The first cells run offline. They test empty queries, the Google results
parser, URL normalization, RRF, BM25,
[`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus), bot
wall detection, region inference, backend parameters,
[`page_date`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#page_date)
and the shape of a
[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
result. The later cells run real searches and are skipped by the tests.
Their saved output shows what each call returns.

``` python
# An empty query does nothing and uses no network.
assert search('') == []
assert research('')['sources'] == []
assert rrf([]) == [] and rerank('x', []) == []

# Parse Google results from static data without a browser or network.
_serp = ('<html><body><div class="MjjYud"><div class="g">'
         '<a href="https://ex.com/p"><h3>Example Page</h3></a>'
         '<div class="VwiC3b">A short snippet.</div></div></div>'
         '<div><a href="https://www.google.com/aclk"><h3>Ad</h3></a></div></body></html>')
_g = _parse_google(_serp, 5)
assert len(_g) == 1, f'expected 1 organic result, got {len(_g)}'   # Filter out the google.com ad link.
assert _g[0]['href'] == 'https://ex.com/p' and _g[0]['title'] == 'Example Page'
assert _g[0]['content'] == 'A short snippet.'
```

``` python
# Treat URLs with these differences as one page.
assert norm_url('https://www.x.com/a/?utm_source=t#frag') == norm_url('http://x.com/a')
assert norm_url('https://x.com/a') != norm_url('https://x.com/b')

_g = [dict(href='https://x.com/1', rank=1, engine='google'), dict(href='https://x.com/8', rank=8, engine='google')]
_b = [dict(href='https://x.com/8', rank=8, engine='brave'),  dict(href='https://x.com/2', rank=2, engine='brave')]

# One result from each backend keeps the better-ranked result first.
_solo = rrf([_g[:1], _b[1:]])
assert [h['href'] for h in _solo] == ['https://x.com/1', 'https://x.com/2'], _solo

# Agreement across backends can outrank one strong hit.
_f = rrf([_g, _b])
assert _f[0]['href'] == 'https://x.com/8' and _f[0]['engines'] == ['google', 'brave']
assert len(_f) == 3                                                    # Remove duplicates across backends.

# Do not promote a domain without a rank.
_w = rrf([[dict(href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust', rank=7, engine='google'),
           dict(href='https://actix.rs/', rank=1, engine='google')]])
assert _w[0]['href'] == 'https://actix.rs/', _w
```

``` python
# BM25 ranks the document that covers the query terms.
_docs = ['sqlite wal mode benchmark write ahead log', 'a recipe for banana bread', 'wal mode']
_s = bm25('sqlite wal mode benchmark', _docs)
assert _s[0] == max(_s) and _s[1] == 0.0, _s

# Reranking moves the relevant hit above a higher-scoring irrelevant hit.
_hits = [dict(href='https://a.com/cake', title='Banana bread', body='baking', score=1.0),
         dict(href='https://b.com/sqlite-wal-benchmark', title='SQLite WAL benchmark', body='wal vs journal', score=0.9)]
assert rerank('sqlite wal benchmark', _hits, method='lexical')[0]['href'].startswith('https://b.com')

# `focus()` keeps the passage that answers the query.
_md = ('Cookie notice. We use cookies.\n\n' + 'Navigation menu home about contact.\n\n'*8 +
       'WAL mode allows readers and writers to proceed concurrently, unlike the rollback journal.\n\n' +
       'Subscribe to our newsletter.\n\n'*8)
_f = focus(_md, 'wal mode concurrent readers writers', chars=200)
assert 'concurrently' in _f and len(_f) <= 260, _f
assert 'concurrently' not in _md[:200]      # Head truncation would miss this passage.
```

# A Cloudflare interstitial can have status 200. Do not add it to the corpus.
class _P:
    def __init__(self, status=200, html=''): self.status, self.html_content, self.html = status, html, html
assert not usable(_P(200, '<html><head><title>Just a moment...</title></head><body>Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue</body></html>'))
assert not usable(_P(403, '<html>' + 'x'*500 + '</html>'))
assert not usable(None)
assert usable(_P(200, '<html><body>' + 'real prose about sqlite. '*40 + '</body></html>'))
assert _why(_P(429)) == 'http 429' and _why(None) == 'fetch failed'
```

# Country and language are separate answers.
assert infer_country('rebuild my garage in australia') == 'au'
assert infer_country('garage rebuild sydney quotes') == 'au'           # Cities count.
assert infer_country('planning permission in the UK') == 'uk'
assert infer_country('compare australia and germany building codes') is None   # A query naming two countries returns neither.
assert infer_country('garage rebuild cost') is None
assert infer_country('give us a quote') is None                        # Bare 'us' is the pronoun.
assert infer_country('australianism') is None                          # Match whole words.

assert infer_language('what is the best way to do this for my house') == 'en'
assert infer_language('welche Vorschriften gelten für eine Garage in Österreich') == 'de'
assert infer_language('garage') is None                                # One word is not enough evidence.
assert infer_language('la') is None                                    # This word occurs in several languages.

# Use the country from the subject and the language from the asker.
assert infer_region('I want to rebuild my garage in australia, what is the regulation') == 'au-en'
assert infer_region('garage rebuild sydney') == 'au-en'
assert infer_region('do I need planning permission for a garage in the UK') == 'uk-en'
assert infer_region('what is the cost of living in france') == 'fr-en'  # Use the French country code and English language code.
assert infer_region('welche Vorschriften gelten für eine Garage in Österreich') == 'at-de'
assert infer_region('aktuelle KI Regulierung Österreich Unternehmen 2026') == 'at-de'  # Use the country's language when no function words occur.
assert infer_region('compare australia and germany building codes') == 'us-en'         # Use the default when the country is unclear.
assert infer_region('garage rebuild cost') == 'us-en'
assert infer_region('', dflt='au-en') == 'au-en' and infer_region(None) == 'us-en'
assert _region('garage in australia', 'uk-en') == 'uk-en'              # Use the explicit region.

# Pass `region` and `timelimit` to every backend.
_calls = []
def _spy(be, q, region='us-en', page=1, timeout=8, tries=2, **kw):
    _calls.append(dict(be=be, region=region, **kw))
    return [dict(title=be, href=f'https://e.com/{be}', body='', engine=be, rank=1)]
_real, _engine_hits = _engine_hits, _spy
try:
    search('sqlite wal mode', timelimit='y')
    assert [c['timelimit'] for c in _calls] == ['y']*len(TEXT_BACKENDS), _calls
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'us-en'}

    _calls.clear(); search('rebuild my garage in australia')
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'au-en'}, _calls
    assert not any('timelimit' in c for c in _calls)          # Omit the value so ddgs uses its default.

    _calls.clear(); search('garage in australia', region='uk-en', timelimit='m', safesearch='off')
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'uk-en'}
    assert all(c['timelimit'] == 'm' and c['safesearch'] == 'off' for c in _calls)

    _calls.clear(); assert search('  ') == [] and _calls == []
finally: _engine_hits = _real
```

``` python
# `cache=` keeps results for the same call. It does not keep empty results. `forget()` clears the cache.
from fossick.core import forget
_calls, _empty = [], [False]
def _spy(be, q, region='us-en', page=1, timeout=8, tries=2, **kw):
    _calls.append(be)
    return [] if _empty[0] else [dict(title=be, href=f'https://e.com/{be}', body='', engine=be, rank=1)]
_real, _engine_hits = _engine_hits, _spy
try:
    forget()
    a = search('sqlite wal mode', cache=60); asked = len(_calls)
    assert a and search('sqlite wal mode', cache=60) is a and len(_calls) == asked   # Return the cached result.
    search('sqlite wal mode', n=3, cache=60); assert len(_calls) == 2*asked          # Different arguments cause another request.
    search('sqlite wal mode'); assert len(_calls) == 3*asked                         # The default disables caching.
    forget(); search('sqlite wal mode', cache=60); assert len(_calls) == 4*asked
    _empty[0] = True; _calls.clear()
    assert search('nothing here', cache=60) == [] and search('nothing here', cache=60) == []
    assert len(_calls) == 2*asked                                                    # An empty result is not cached.
finally: _engine_hits = _real; forget()
```

    fossick: search('nothing here') got nothing: every backend returned nothing

``` python
# `page_date` reads JSON-LD, `<meta>` tags, `<time>` elements and URLs.
class _D:
    def __init__(self, html='', url=''): self.html, self.url = html, url

_ld = lambda s: _D(f'<script type="application/ld+json">{s}</script>')
assert page_date(_ld('{"@type":"Article","datePublished":"2024-03-07T09:00:00Z"}')) == '2024-03-07'
assert page_date(_ld('{"@graph":[{"@type":"WebSite"},{"datePublished":"2019-11-02"}]}')) == '2019-11-02'
assert page_date(_ld('{"datePublished":"not a date","dateModified":"2024-05-05"}')) == '2024-05-05'
assert page_date(_D('<meta property="article:published_time" content="2022-06-15T10:11:12+00:00">')) == '2022-06-15'
assert page_date(_D('<meta name="DC.date.issued" content="2021-1-5">')) == '2021-01-05'
assert page_date(_D('<meta name="viewport" content="width=1"><meta name="date" content="2025-12-31">')) == '2025-12-31'
assert page_date(_D('<time datetime="2023-08-01">last August</time>')) == '2023-08-01'
assert page_date(_D('', 'https://blog.example.com/2018/09/wal-mode')) == '2018-09-01'   # Use day 01 when only the month is present.
assert page_date(_D('<p>nothing dated here</p>', 'https://e.com/x')) is None

# A malformed JSON-LD block must not hide a later meta tag.
assert page_date(_D('<script type="application/ld+json">{oops</script>'
                    '<meta name="pubdate" content="2020-02-29">')) == '2020-02-29'

# Prefer the longest month and day alternatives.
assert _iso('2019-11-02') == '2019-11-02' and _iso('2025-12-31') == '2025-12-31'
assert _iso('v1.2 build 7') is None
```
